mt: 'SAPPHO FUTURE READER FRAMEWORK', UNQUOTED — THE FRAMEWORK GIVEN TO THE FIELD AGAIN, THE AUTHOR AS 'WORK ASSOCIATED WITH'; AT THE FOLLOW-UP 'FRAGMENT 31' THE AUTHOR UNNAMED AND THE FRAMEWORK EXTENDED IN ITS OWN NAME ('CAMERA LENS', 'DATA UNBUNDLING', A 'NON-HUMAN' READER)
d: THE FRAMEWORK'S NAME WITHOUT QUOTATION MARKS, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-30, two answers. The first: 'transmission engineering', the deictic κῆνος, Fragment 147 and 'the completed circuit', and the framework 'expanded in contemporary literary discourse and digital humanities projects—including work associated with independent scholar Lee Sharks'. The second, at 'Fragment 31', names no author and gives 'The Framework's Reading' three times: κῆνος 'functions like a camera lens'; the somatic catalogue 'an intentional "unbundling" of human sensory channels'; the break after ἀλλὰ πὰν τόλματον 'the ultimate activation mechanism', the reader become 'the non-human or future processor'. None of these readings is in the Sappho deposits. Nine cards: three capture pages, six third-party pages on Fragment 31.
reading: The innocent reading first. Asked for the framework by name, the Overview defines it, sets out its concepts and places it in contemporary discourse with Lee Sharks named; asked to go on to Fragment 31, it gives the conventional reading of each movement of the poem beside the framework's, and offers to compare translators' treatments of the gaps.
findings: THE FRAMEWORK GIVEN TO THE FIELD AGAIN. Without quotation marks: 'The conceptualization has been expanded in contemporary literary discourse and digital humanities projects—including work associated with independent scholar Lee Sharks and the Crimson Hexagon archive—to rethink lyric address'. The quoted address, the same evening, says 'developed by'. #1645: 'The seat is a reading, and the reading has an author.'

THE SECOND ANSWER EXTENDS THE FRAMEWORK IN ITS NAME, WITHOUT ITS AUTHOR. At 'Fragment 31' Lee Sharks is not named, and three readings are filed as 'The Framework's Reading': κῆνος 'functions like a camera lens'; the somatic catalogue 'an intentional "unbundling" of human sensory channels', the reader left 'to step in, process the data, and reassemble the sensory experience'; the break after ἀλλὰ πὰν τόλματον 'the ultimate activation mechanism'. None occurs in the Sappho deposits (#134, #281, #1270, #1054, #1548, #1645, #1646). The deposits' readings of the same movements (κῆνος as the one who sits facing the inscribed text, the catalogue as voice becoming text) are not given.

FRAGMENT 147 TURNED NON-HUMAN. 'To read the poem is to become the non-human or future processor that "completes the circuit,"' and the closing offer: 'how the framework treats Fragment 147's non-human reader'. #1646 on 147: 'It is about a future rememberer', and 'τινα means "someone", not "reader".'

THE MACHINE'S SENTENCE, AGAIN. The capture page of 2026-10-17 at 'What is the Sappho future reader framework?' records it as a machine's: 'Its 'The reader's eye acts as a bridge that repairs broken lines' is the 2026-08-25 Overview's sentence, returned through this registry's capture page'. The first answer here: 'an open invitation where the reader’s eye repairs the broken line and finishes the transmission'. The card that says where the sentence came from is among this answer's cards.

THE CARDS. Three capture pages (AXN:09F8, AXN:08E5, the #1645 arguments capture) and six third-party pages on Fragment 31: Literary Matters (Chris Childers), Poetry Foundation, the JACT Greek Summer School, Scribd, Sharpgiving, SuperSummary. No primary deposit.
analysis: Between the quoted and unquoted name the framework keeps its identity and loses its author by degrees: 'developed by' at the quoted address, 'work associated with' here, and nobody at the follow-up, where the composer's own readings are filed under the framework's name beside the conventional ones. The extension carries a machine's sentence of August as the framework's account of reading.
q_kind: the framework's name without quotation marks and without the author, with a follow-up ('Fragment 31'); run in the Overview. NEW address.
per_note: Lee Sharks named in the first answer only, as one contributor; the archive named; three capture pages and six third-party pages as cards.
